entries.speaker: Ryuji
entries.en: So, our reputation'll go up if we can win[n]coins, right?

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Since these are all games of chance,[n]I wouldn't be surprised to find they were[n]tampered with.

entries.speaker: Ann
entries.en: If that's the case, won't we lose every[n]time until we figure it out?

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Of course. Especially considering this[n]world belongs to Sae-san, a public[n]prosecutor.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: This place appears to be a casino, but[n]it is in fact a courthouse, correct?

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: The chance of being found guilty upon[n]first trial in Japan is 99.9%. It is the[n]highest in the world.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: If a person is arrested and a case is made[n]against them, they have almost no hope[n]of winning.

entries.speaker: Ann
entries.en: How can a percentage like that really be[n]possible? Are the investigations accurate?

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: No... The investigators are human too,[n]after all.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: You are not the first to point out[n]the rigged nature of this system.[n]The prosecution is near unbeatable.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: That's why cases of false accusation[n]cause such a stir: they are exceedingly[n]rare.

entries.speaker: Ryuji
entries.en: But it's total bullshit gettin' arrested[n]even when you're not guilty!

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: And if we do not hurry, the Phantom[n]Thieves will fall victim to a similar fate.

entries.speaker: Makoto
entries.en: ...We're going to win this, no matter what.
